A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAIL-VL research. Their main text, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, scaling experiments, training-stage ablations and caption-quality evaluations, including Tables 2–6.

after.justification: v2 reports original 2B and 8B benchmark results, scaling experiments, caption/OCR controls and caption-quality evaluations, including Tables 3–6 and 8–9.

M1.justification: The four-step caption-curation pipeline and five-stage parameter-unfreezing and curriculum-SFT procedure remain intact. The larger model configuration and newly documented pixel-shuffle component do not establish a change to the underlying algorithm, objective or inference procedure.

E1.justification: v2 removes LLaVABench from quantitative evaluation and replaces the earlier LLaVABench showcases with new English/Chinese 8B examples. The other 18 VQA benchmarks and Appendix D's bilingual caption/OCR suite remain. Increasing SAIL-Caption's sample count does not itself introduce new task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds InternVL2.5-MPO to the 2B comparison and Figure 5, and BLIP3-KALE to caption-quality and pretraining comparisons. Earlier 2B competitors remain in Table 8; Table 9 adds comparisons with larger counterparts of the baseline families.

E3.justification: The stated 2B alignment/advance budgets change from 16B/131B to 131B/524B tokens, while SAIL-Caption grows from 100M to 300M images. v2 adds 8B experiments with 20B/32B-token budgets and introduces OCR quality/repetition controls. The overall evaluation average covers 18 rather than 19 benchmarks, and the separate OpenCompass-average metric is removed.

E4.justification: v1's leave-one-training-stage-out ablation in Section 5.1 and Table 3 is removed. v2 adds alignment-stage scaling analysis and OCR quality/repetition studies, extends advance-stage scaling, and revises existing SFT/AIO and data-composition analyses. The correlation study is retained in Appendix E, while model showcases are replaced and caption comparisons gain KALE cases.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and use Pearson correlation and R², without run-count disclosures, uncertainty intervals or significance tests. v2's separately reported correlation values for the two SFT datasets extend the results using the same statistical practice.

E6.justification: v1 reports a 2B average of 68.6 over 19 benchmarks; v2 reports 69.1 over 18 under revised training and adds an 8B average of 74.5. These averages do not establish a same-setting gain. Updated 2B results are mixed, including ChartQA 79.6 to 81.0 and OCRBench 835 to 806. Scaling, caption-quality and composition results also change; the earlier correlation summary of ρ=0.91 and R²=0.83 becomes separate summaries of 0.97/0.94 and 0.99/0.98 in Appendix E.

T1.justification: Both versions present empirical scaling curves and correlations without formal scaling theorems or proofs. No substantive mathematical definition, formal assumption or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The central contributions—caption curation, data-size scaling and curriculum SFT—remain. v2 broadens the headline SOTA claim from one 2B model to a 2B/8B series and updates the claimed benchmark comparison from 19 to 18 benchmarks.

C2.justification: v2 attributes the effectiveness of repeated high-quality OCR data to frozen-LLM pretraining mitigating overfitting, and qualifies the narrower 8B advantage by its limited training budget. It reframes curriculum scaling around data complexity and removes v1's explanation linking caption-subset statistics to duplicated visual elements.

D1.justification: New Table 2 specifies stage-specific resolutions, visual-token limits, trainable parameters, batch sizes and learning rates. v2 also discloses the 2M-sample annealing data size, HDFS streaming and updated 2B/8B computation costs; earlier framework and hardware details are retained in Appendix F. Model-release information expands to the series, and Appendix C announces a future caption-subset release.

R1.justification: v2 adds BLIP3-KALE and World2Seq to the recaptioning discussion, explains KALE's caption-generation lineage, and adds original references for retained benchmarks. The overall research positioning and three related-work subsections remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and Sections 2–3 are substantially rewritten and compressed, including merged training-stage descriptions and revised curriculum terminology. Correlation analysis and implementation details move to Appendices E/F, Appendices B/C exchange order, and the acknowledgments are removed.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned and the scaling panels are reorganized. v2 adds a training-recipe table, restructures the main results into adjacent 2B/8B comparisons, adds full appendix result tables and removes the stage-ablation table. Caption showcases expand into a full-page comparison, model showcases are replaced, and the correlation figure moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v2's stage-specific training recipe and Appendix F improve reproducibility, while expanded scaling experiments, 8B comparisons and OCR quality/repetition controls strengthen empirical support. These gains are tempered by removal of v1's stage-removal ablation, which weakens direct evidence for the five-stage design. The changed benchmark suite also prevents treating the higher 2B average as a direct performance gain.
